items.title: Learning from Nature: A Biomimetic Network Framework for Occupational Health and Safety Research
items.abstract: Occupational health and safety research has long relied on two ways of understanding harm. One traces the chain of conditions behind an accident, and the other forecasts the outcome of an incident from large bodies of recorded cases. Both treat the factors surrounding an incident as inputs pointing toward a result. Neither was built to ask how the categories of risk in a whole body of records are organized in relation to one another, independent of any single outcome. This paper addresses that gap through biomimicry, taking the way living systems organize their interactions as a template for reading how risk is organized in safety data. Ecologists have long described how two distinct sets of entities connect through bipartite networks, and they have developed a compact set of measures for reading the structure of those networks, covering whether interactions concentrate in a shared core or separate into compartments, which categories are specialized and which dominate, and how a system responds when its parts are removed. Occupational safety data fit this biological template, because the categorical fields that safety agencies record pair naturally into the same two-set form. Transferring these ecological measures to safety records, this study sets out how the measures map onto safety questions and illustrates their use across construction, mining, manufacturing, and healthcare. A worked example then applies the full procedure to a public dataset of 158,396 healthcare injury records, building the bipartite matrices and reading their nestedness, modularity, specialization, and robustness against a null model, which shows that the approach runs end to end on real administrative data. The study presents this as a proposed framework and a demonstration of its feasibility rather than a validated method and argues that this nature-derived structural reading complements rather than replaces the causal and predictive traditions.

items.title: Legal Protection for Bank Employees in the Era of Digitalization: A Normative Legal Analysis of Indonesian Labor Law and OJK Regulations
items.abstract: The rapid digitalization of the banking sector has transformed work structures, performance evaluation systems, and employment relations. While regulatory frameworks primarily emphasize consumer protection and financial system stability, limited attention has been given to legal protection for bank employees affected by digital transformation. This study examines legal protection for bank workers in the era of banking digitalization by analyzing its alignment with Indonesian labor law, Financial Services Authority (OJK) regulations, Bank Indonesia’s payment system policy, and personal data protection principles. Using normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and analytical approaches, this article analyzes secondary legal materials and scholarly literature related to algorithmic management, digital surveillance, electronic performance monitoring, and workplace data governance. The analysis identifies three central issues: the transformation of work roles and performance targets, intensified digital surveillance, and unequal access to digital competency development. The study indicates a regulatory gap between labor law provisions and sectoral financial regulations, particularly regarding algorithmic transparency, workplace privacy, employee data protection, and psychosocial protection. It concludes that legal protection must be expanded through adaptive regulatory harmonization, human review of system-based employment decisions, proportional limits on workplace surveillance, and stronger protection of employee personal data.

items.title: LEVERAGING ICT AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-ENHANCED SYSTEMS TO IMPROVE STUDENT ENGAGEMENT AND COGNITIVE OUTCOMES
items.abstract: This study examined the association between the use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enhanced systems, student engagement and academic performance among tertiary students in Nigeria. A cross-sectional correlational survey design was adopted. Questionnaires were administered to 200 students of Kwara State College of Education, Ilorin, and 184 usable responses (92%) were analyzed alongside academic records obtained from institutional files. Data were collected with a 30-item, 4-point Likert questionnaire (Cronbach's α = 0.85) and analyzed with SPSS using descriptive statistics, an independent samples t-test, and regression-based mediation analysis. Students reported high behavioural (M = 3.34) and emotional (M = 3.24) engagement, and moderate-high cognitive engagement (M = 3.14). Students with higher weekly use of adaptive learning platforms, intelligent tutoring systems and educational chatbots had higher mean academic scores (72.4%) than low-usage peers (66.8%), t(182) = 3.58, p < .001, d = 0.61 (medium effect). Student engagement partially mediated the statistical relationship between ICT/AI use and academic performance. The most frequently reported barriers were infrastructure limitations (88.0%), digital literacy gaps (53.8%), and cognitive overload or offloading (38.0%). Because the data are cross-sectional and drawn from a single institution, the findings indicate associations rather than causal effects and should be generalized with caution. The study recommends investment in reliable power and affordable connectivity, capacity building for lecturers and students, pedagogically guided AI use, and context-appropriate low-bandwidth tools.

items.title: Lipid nanoparticle platforms for p53-targeted cancer therapy
items.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as the most clinically validated nanocarrier platform in oncology, transitioning from liposomal chemotherapy to the cornerstone of mRNA-based therapeutics. This review critically examines the evolving LNP landscape with a deliberate focus on p53, the tumour suppressor directly mutated or functionally silenced via pathway dysregulation in over half of human cancers and a unifying therapeutic target across diverse tumour types. We analyse LNP platform design, physicochemical properties, and structure-activity relationships that govern encapsulation, stability, and release. A dedicated section synthesizes p53-directed nucleic acid strategies delivered by LNPs, including p53 mRNA for wild-type restoration, siRNA for mutant p53 silencing, miR-34a mimics engaging the p53 downstream axis, and CRISPR-Cas9 components for TP53 correction. The review evaluates passive and active targeting, stimuli-responsive release mechanisms responsive to tumour microenvironmental cues, and the integration of p53 nanotherapy with immune checkpoint blockade. Clinical translation is appraised through key 2020–2026 milestones, notably the KEYNOTE-942 trial of personalized neoantigen mRNA-4157, which clinically validates the mRNA-LNP platform in oncology, alongside emerging preclinical and early exploratory p53 mRNA-LNP programs in hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and pancreatic cancer. Persistent challenges, including liver-dominant biodistribution, anti-PEG immunogenicity, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory complexity, are discussed alongside artificial intelligence-guided lipid discovery and biomimetic approaches. By reframing LNP development around p53 biology, this review highlights how tumour-suppressor restoration offers a mechanistically coherent strategy to enhance therapeutic index, reprogram the tumour immune microenvironment, and extend LNP clinical benefit beyond the liver compartment across diverse tumour types. The synthesis indicates that p53-focused LNP engineering represents a convergent opportunity to unify diverse cancer nanomedicine efforts under a single, biologically grounded therapeutic paradigm.

items.title: Low‐Field MRI for Knee Imaging: Current Insights and Evidence From a Systematic Review
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Low‐field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has regained interest for musculoskeletal imaging due to advances in magnet design, hardware optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)–based reconstruction, offering improved accessibility, patient comfort, and sustainability. Purpose This systematic review aimed to explore and summarize the current status of low‐field MRI for knee investigations. Study Type Systematic review on MEDLINE, Cinhal, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases. PROSPERO protocol (CRD42024544354). Population Approximately 3400 participants (8–89 years) encompassing healthy volunteers, community‐based cohorts, and patients with diverse knee pathologies were evaluated. Few studies incorporate phantom experiments. Field Strength/Sequence This review covered a range of very‐low‐field (< 0.1 T), conventional low‐field (0.1‐< 0.29 T), and upper‐range low‐field (> 0.3 T–0.55 T) with standard, extremity, open, and weight‐bearing/standing systems. SE/FSE and GRE sequences, 3D GRE quantitative protocols, and AI‐based were used. Assessment Two reviewers independently extracted data on knee protocols, technical parameters, diagnostic performance, and reported advantages and limitations. Statistical Tests Study quality was assessed using appropriate JBI critical appraisal tools. A narrative synthesis and descriptive analysis of the findings from the included studies are provided due to the heterogeneity of the intervention and outcome. Results From 3726 records, 31 were included. Low‐field MRI demonstrated high diagnostic performance for meniscal and ligamentous injuries but lower sensitivity for early cartilage degeneration. Weight‐bearing MRI provided distinct functional information but not direct equivalence to standard MRI. AI‐enhanced reconstruction was evaluated in a limited number of single‐center, vendor‐specific studies and was associated with improved image quality and diagnostic confidence. Important limitations included lower signal‐to‐noise ratio, reduced spatial resolution, protocol heterogeneity, and limited pathology‐validated evidence. Data Conclusion Low‐field MRI may provide a clinically useful complementary option for selected knee meniscal and ligamentous indications. However, heterogeneous evidence, influenced by field strength, scanner design, sequences, and reference standards, limits claims of equivalence with high‐field MRI, particularly for subtle cartilage lesions. Advances in hardware and AI have improved image quality and efficiency; however, evidence is limited and larger standardized multicenter studies are required. Evidence Level 5. Technical Efficacy Stage 5.

items.title: Luxury fashion brands’ AI-powered sustainability chatbot communication: how information qualities and brand luxury perception shape consumer trust and behavior
items.abstract: This study examines how sustainability communication in luxury retail shapes brand trust and behavioral intentions, focusing on consumers' post-exposure perceptions of information quality and provider type. Building on perceived objectivity and perceived persuasiveness, the study explores how consumers evaluate identical sustainability information attributed to either a human agent or an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot, and how these perceptions influence brand trust, information acceptance intention, and purchase intention. A scenario-based experiment with 346 participants was conducted, and the data were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Perceived objectivity and perceived persuasiveness were positively associated with brand trust, which inturn mediated their relationships with information acceptance intention and purchase intention. The indirect effect of perceived objectivity was significant only under AI communication, suggesting that algorithmic provider cues may strengthen the trust-mediated role of objectivity, whereas perceived persuasiveness remained consistently associated with trust and behavioral intentions across provider types. Subgroup analyses further suggest a conditional pattern: among consumers with lower perceived brand luxury, the links between brand trust and behavioral intentions were stronger under AI communication, whereas no significant provider differences emerged among those with higher perceived brand luxury. As these results derivefrom split-sample multi-group comparisons rather than a formal interaction test, they should be regarded as subgroup-based evidence. These findings extend luxury branding research by showing how AI provider cues shape perceived information quality in sustainability communication and by highlighting the need to align provider strategy with consumers' perceptions of luxury brands.

items.title: Machine Learning for Solar Thermal Energy Optimization and Smart Control
items.abstract: This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.

items.title: Making blue carbon governable in China: standardisation, local experimentation and policy implications
items.abstract: China’s dual-carbon agenda has elevated blue carbon from a broad ecological aspiration to an actionable policy domain requiring accounting standards, measurement, reporting and verification (MRV), and institutional implementation pathways. This article examines how blue carbon policies are made operational in China, focusing on the institutional and technical devices through which marine carbon sinks are rendered calculable, verifiable and governable. Drawing on Jasanoff’s notion of sociotechnical imaginaries, it treats blue carbon not as a pre-given natural–technical object, but as a policy object iteratively defined, quantified, verified and recalibrated through policy narratives, standardisation, methodological rule-making and local experimentation. Methodologically, the study combines thematic analysis of national and coastal local policy documents, standards, accounting guidelines and regional methodologies with semi-structured interviews with 12 domain experts across policy, research and market-facing practice. Four findings emerge. First, blue carbon is constructed as a governable climate space, with standardisation functioning as metrological infrastructure. Second, implementation follows a two-wheel structure in which national policy direction and unified accounting grammars are made operable through local devices such as platforms, carbon-inclusion schemes, funds, insurance and judicial compensation. Third, market-facing implementation depends less on willingness to trade than on whether methodologies and MRV systems can institutionalise uncertainty into verifiable rules at bearable cost. Fourth, structural bottlenecks—cross-department coordination, uneven local capacity and unresolved risk allocation—shape credibility and scalability. The article contributes a mechanism-oriented account of how blue carbon moves from policy ambition to institutional operation under uncertainty.

items.title: MANAGEMENT MODEL FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BASED ON EUROPEAN EXPERIENCE
items.abstract: The article focuses on the development of a management model for the implementation of artificial intelligence technologies in Ukrainian industry, aimed at ensuring a transition from an enterprise’s technological and organizational readiness to measurable performance outcomes from the use of artificial intelligence. The relevance of the study is determined by the need to accelerate the digital transformation of Ukraine’s industrial sector under conditions of limited financial and human resources, energy-related risks, changes in production chains, and the gradual integration of Ukrainian enterprises into the European digital environment. The study systematizes the key prerequisites that determine an enterprise’s capacity to use artificial intelligence technologies, including the state of technological infrastructure, data quality and accessibility, organizational conditions, staff competencies, economic capabilities, and interaction with the external digital environment. The necessity of distinguishing between the concepts of artificial intelligence readiness, artificial intelligence implementation, and artificial intelligence performance is substantiated. The proposed approach provides not only for the possibility of scaling a solution but also for returning to the stage of use-case selection to adjust the selected scenario or terminate the project in cases of insufficient performance. The practical significance of the obtained results lies in the possibility of applying the proposed management logic by managers and specialists of industrial enterprises when developing a portfolio of digital initiatives, selecting artificial intelligence projects, determining criteria for their piloting, and making decisions on scaling. Particular attention is paid to the European experience of using artificial intelligence in industry, particularly in energy, semiconductor manufacturing, automotive manufacturing, and industrial automation, which makes it possible to identify directions for adapting such experience to Ukrainian conditions. The study results in a management model that integrates enterprise readiness, practical technology implementation, assessment of the achieved effect, management decision-making, and subsequent performance into a unified cyclical process.

items.title: Mapping hybrid Infotech competencies for workplace learning: a bibliometric taxonomy and theoretical framework
items.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the growing demand for hybrid information technology (IT) roles that blend technical, strategic, and cognitive skills. It proposes a theoretical Nomological Framework that conceptualizes how multidisciplinary competencies may connect digital transformation with organisational outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A rigorous three-stage analytical procedure was employed, involving data normalization of 114 Scopus-indexed articles, mathematical clustering via VOSviewer to identify thematic patterns, and theoretical synthesis grounded in the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory. Findings The study proposes a taxonomy of hybrid IT competencies and a nomological framework that categorizes multidisciplinary competencies and their development approaches. Four competency domains, Foundational (Red), Strategic (Green), Synergistic (Yellow), and Cognitive (Blue), offer a structured basis for developing future-ready IT professionals in the digital workplace. Research limitations/implications By moving beyond simple skill-listing, the proposed taxonomy provides a theoretical basis for examining competency transitions. It provides a structure for understanding how human capital fosters resilience in volatile digital markets. Practical implications The findings inform the design of evidence-based workplace learning and competency development initiatives. By linking competency domains with appropriate development approaches, the study supports organizations and educators in creating effective upskilling and lifelong learning pathways for the digital workforce. Originality/value The study contributes a bibliometrically derived taxonomy that integrates technical, behavioral, strategic and cognitive competency perspectives within the emerging hybrid IT context.

items.title: Mapping the Evolving Landscape of Ransomware Research: A Bibliometric Analysis for Cybersecurity Advancements
items.abstract: Ransomware is a critical cybersecurity threat that disrupts healthcare, finance, and government by encrypting data and demanding ransom. Although narrative and systematic reviews have examined ransomware from technical, sector-specific, and legal perspectives, quantitative bibliometric mapping remains scarce, and existing studies cover shorter periods and fewer analytical techniques. This study addresses that gap through a bibliometric analysis of 1,386 ransomware-related publications indexed in Scopus from 2007 to 2024, using Scopus, BiblioMagika, VOSviewer, Publish or Perish, and Bibliometrix. It examines publication trends, leading authors, institutions, countries, thematic clusters, and collaboration patterns. Results show a sharp rise in output since 2017, though only seven researchers have published ten or more papers on the topic. Keyword and thematic-map patterns point to early detection techniques, deep learning, data breach analysis, convolutional neural networks, feature selection, machine learning, and artificial intelligence as areas of growing activity, consistent with a shift toward proactive and intelligent defense mechanisms. By mapping the intellectual structure and evolution of ransomware research, this study offers insights for cybersecurity professionals, academics, and policymakers seeking to understand current trends, anticipate future challenges, and design more effective mitigation strategies.

items.title: Mapping The Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Group Creative Processes: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is finding its way into creative work at a growing pace, yet its specific role within collaborative creative processes, those involving multiple people working together, remains poorly understood and fragmented across the literature. This scoping review maps the empirical research on integrating GenAI into group creative processes, outlining creative domains, tasks, AI tools, AI roles, stages of integration, and reported outcomes. Following PRISMA-ScR and JBI guidance, a systematic search was conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, and PsycINFO. Empirical peer-reviewed studies were included when they involved at least two human participants engaged in a collaborative creative process supported by GenAI. Thirty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria. The majority were conducted in educational and design contexts, with brainstorming, content creation, and design development emerging as the most frequent task types. GenAI was most often integrated as a co-creative partner, typically during the ideation stage or across multiple phases of the creative process. Reported benefits included enhanced ideation, greater efficiency, improved engagement, and stronger collaboration quality, while the main tensions revolved around over-reliance on AI, cognitive offloading, homogenization of ideas, and unresolved questions of authorship and agency. Taken together, the findings suggest that GenAI is becoming an active component of hybrid human–AI creative systems, but whether its benefits are realized depends heavily on how collaborative workflows are designed to preserve human agency, support critical reflection, and maintain diversity of perspectives.

items.title: Measuring Wikipedia Quality at Scale: Assessment of Content, Information Sources, Data Visualizations
items.abstract: This presentation provides an overview of research on the large-scale, automated assessment of Wikipedia quality across multiple language editions. It explores how artificial intelligence, natural language processing, machine learning, citation analysis, internal link networks, image classification, and composite quality indicators can support the evaluation of encyclopedic content, information sources, and data visualizations.The presentation covers several interconnected research areas, including multilingual article quality assessment, sentiment analysis using traditional and large language models, the analysis of links between Wikipedia articles, the evaluation of web sources cited in Wikipedia, and the assessment of data visualizations such as maps, charts, tables, and diagrams. It also introduces research-based tools, including WikiRank.net and BestRef.net, which support the exploration of article quality and information source usage across language editions and topics.Particular attention is given to methodological challenges, including differences between language editions, model selection, topic-dependent biases, the interpretation of community-generated quality signals, and the limitations of automated evaluation methods.The presentation also features Wikipedia-Map.net, an interactive platform for exploring connections between Wikipedia articles, publicly demonstrated for the first time at an event of this kind.Overall, the presentation illustrates how computational approaches can help identify knowledge gaps, support content improvement, and advance our understanding of information quality in open, collaborative knowledge ecosystems.Presented at: Open Knowledge: Wikimedia & Research in the CEE Region, 9-10 October 2026, Katowice, Poland

items.title: Medical publishing in the era of artificial intelligence
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into medical research and publishing represents a transformative shift, offering unprecedented opportunities to streamline workflow efficiency, enhance language clarity, and accelerate scientific dissemination. However, this rapid technological adoption introduces ethical, epistemological, and procedural challenges, including concerns over data fabrication, automated bias, intellectual property infringement, and the erosion of scholarly accountability. A structured analysis of practical applications highlights a clear demarcation between acceptable supplementary uses and strictly prohibited practices. AI tools are unacceptable as co-authors, as authorship demands moral, legal, and scholarly accountability that non-human entities cannot possess. Similarly, generating or modifying clinical images and media using AI remains unacceptable due to the risk of data distortion and misrepresentation. Within the editorial domain, AI systems must not replace peer reviewers or editorial decision-makers. Uploading confidential manuscript content into external AI platforms violates author confidentiality, while automated algorithms lack the contextual judgment and critical reasoning necessary for peer evaluation and final publication decisions. Conversely, AI tools are acceptable for planning the structure of a manuscript, language and grammar corrections, translation, quantitative or qualitative data analysis, and formatting, provided their use is transparently disclosed and critically evaluated by human researchers. Ultimately, the ethical deployment of AI in medical literature hinges on the principle that technology must serve as an auxiliary tool rather than a replacement for human cognition. Human authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors retain full responsibility and accountability for the accuracy, integrity, and scientific validity of published work.

items.title: Memoria persistente del agente: el dato que sigue en la siguiente sesión / Persistent agent memory: the data that is still there in the next session
items.abstract: Los asistentes de consumo recuerdan entre sesiones, y los papers de agentes tratan esa memoria como un módulo de capacidad. Este artículo pregunta si esa memoria se documenta como un almacén con controles de escritura, lectura y borrado, o como un estado cuya promesa de olvido no está especificada ni medida. Se leyeron en texto crudo nueve papers, seis páginas de producto de cuatro proveedores y tres textos de autoridades de protección de datos. Las arquitecturas publican recuerdo: con GPT-4, MemGPT pasa del 32,1 % al 92,5 % de accuracy en recuperación profunda y guarda lo desalojado de forma indefinida; LongMemEval midió en agosto de 2024 que ChatGPT con GPT-4o acertaba 0,5773 frente a 0,9184 leyendo el historial completo. Ninguno de esos papers mide el borrado; un benchmark posterior sí lo mide sobre Mem0 y A-Mem como métodos. Los estudios de inserción muestran efectos en prototipos y dependen de su supuesto: AgentPoison asume acceso parcial a la base y logra un ASR medio de al menos el 80 %; MINJA no escribe el banco, pero asume un banco compartido entre usuarios, y obtiene un 76,8 % de ASR medio; en un agente clínico, unas memorias legítimas previas bajan el ASR de GPT-4o-mini del 62 % al 6,67 %. Donde el borrado sí se mide, falla o no es físico: borrar el registro deja la fuga igual que no hacer nada (any-leak 0,86–1,00), y GateMem solo mide olvido en la interfaz. Las fichas ofrecen ver, borrar y apagar, y declaran plazos —30 días para logs de OpenAI, 28 días de inactividad en Copilot Studio— sin prueba de tercero en lo leído. La contribución es separar memoria de tarea y memoria de almacén, y tres estados del borrado: no especificado, especificado y no medido, y medido y fallido. English abstract: Consumer assistants remember across sessions, and agent papers treat that memory as a capability module. This paper asks whether such memory is documented as a store with write, read and deletion controls, or as a state whose promise of forgetting is neither specified nor measured. Nine papers, six product pages from four vendors and three texts from data-protection authorities were read in raw text. The architectures report recall: with GPT-4, MemGPT goes from 32.1% to 92.5% accuracy on deep memory retrieval and keeps evicted messages indefinitely; in August 2024 LongMemEval measured ChatGPT with GPT-4o at 0.5773 versus 0.9184 when reading the full history. None of those papers measures deletion; a later benchmark does measure it on Mem0 and A-Mem as methods. Insertion studies show effects on prototypes and depend on their assumption: AgentPoison assumes partial access to the database and reaches an average ASR of at least 80%; MINJA does not write the bank but assumes a bank shared across users, and obtains an average ASR of 76.8%; in a clinical agent, pre-existing legitimate memories lower GPT-4o-mini's ASR from 62% to 6.67%. Where deletion is measured, it fails or is not physical: deleting the record leaves leakage as if nothing had been done (any-leak 0.86–1.00), and GateMem measures only interface-level forgetting. The help pages offer view, delete and turn off, and state periods—30 days for OpenAI logs, 28 days of inactivity in Copilot Studio—with no third-party test in what was read. The contribution is to separate task memory from store memory, and three states of deletion: not specified, specified but not measured, and measured and failed. Uso de herramientas de IA declarado en el manuscrito; sin conflictos de interés ni financiación.

items.title: Mobile Location-based Recommendation Systems and Local Businesses: Evidence from the Restaurant Industry
items.abstract: We investigate the impact of mobile location-based recommendation systems (MLBRS) on the performance of local businesses. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset of 16,720 restaurants and quasi-experimental variation generated by the official launch of a leading MLBRS, we employ a 2-Stage Least Squares instrumental-variable framework to estimate the effect of algorithmic exposure on consumer engagement. Our analysis reveals that a 1% increase in exposure is associated with a 0.078% increase in clicks; separately, a 1% increase in clicks is associated with a 0.053% increase in visit intentions. Importantly, the estimated exposure effect is larger for geographically disadvantaged restaurants, but primarily at the discovery stage (clicks). This pattern highlights a boundary condition of MLBRS: algorithmic visibility can aid, but it does not by itself resolve the uncertainty involved in acting on a recommendation. Downstream conversion is stronger when restaurants provide richer digital information and reputation signals, including consumer reviews and owner-curated information such as photos and menus. Auxiliary credit-card sales data from a restricted Seoul subsample provide consistent evidence of a positive association between algorithmic exposure and revenue, suggesting that MLBRS can shape the connection of online recommendations to offline economic outcomes.

items.title: Moda algorítmica
items.abstract: This article analyzes how digital platforms, algorithmic systems, and massive data analysis reconfigure the production and circulation of contemporary fashion. It adopts a critical-interpretive qualitative approach, combining systematic literature review, documentary analysis, and examination of empirical cases of platforms such as TikTok and SHEIN. The results evidence the emergence of a sociotechnical regime in which algorithms participate in the identification, amplification, and materialization of aesthetic trends, shifting fashion from a purely symbolic system to a hybrid ecology that articulates cultural practices and computational infrastructures. Tensions are identified between technological innovation and aesthetic standardization, productive acceleration and environmental impacts, concentration of power in platforms and possibilities for creative resistance. It is concluded that algorithmic fashion requires new analytical approaches capable of integrating culture, technology, and governance in the study of contemporary aesthetic transformations.

items.title: Monetisation Models for Academic Creators: A Mixed-Methods Study of 997 Doctorate-Signed Newsletters and 92 Public Discussion Threads
items.abstract: Scholars who publish for the public increasingly try to earn from that work, and generative AI tools promise to cut the hours it takes. This study proposes a mixed-methods framework for describing how academic creators monetise their expertise and how AI tools could change the economics, and applies it to public evidence. A quantitative strand classified the latest posts of 174,656 active newsletters on a large publishing platform, 997 of them signed by authors with a doctoral or professorial title; a qualitative strand coded 92 public question threads with 357 answers in which academics discussed earning from their expertise. One doctorate-signed newsletter in five mentioned an offer of its own, more often than other newsletters in the same topic category (odds ratio 1.47), usually through a single model such as books, courses or paid membership, whereas sponsorship and donations were rare. AI was discussed by 31% of the doctorate-signed newsletters, but only 0.6% described using it in their own work, and naming AI tools was not associated with more offers or more frequent posting. The threads raised employer policy, ethics and tax as the main concerns, and AI appeared in only one of them. A labelled planning simulation suggests that AI drafting mainly saves hours rather than raising income, and pays off most for creators with little time. A protocol for the survey and interviews, with their sample sizes, is proposed.

items.title: Multidimensional effects of a school-based martial arts intervention on physical fitness, executive function, and psychological resilience in adolescents: a quasi-experimental study
items.abstract: Background Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which physical fitness, executive function, and psychological resilience are closely interconnected. School-based martial arts training may provide a multidimensional intervention approach by combining physical exercise, cognitive engagement, self-regulation, and psychosocial development. This study examined the effects of a 12-week school-based martial arts intervention on physical fitness, executive function, psychological resilience, self-regulation, and perceived stress among adolescents. Methods A quasi-experimental repeated-measures design was adopted. A total of 120 adolescents aged 13–16 years from three middle schools in Nanchang, China, were allocated into three groups: School-Based Martial Arts Training Group (SMATG; n = 40), Traditional Physical Education Group (TPEG; n = 40), and Control Group (CG; n = 40). The intervention was conducted three times per week for 60 min per session over 12 weeks. Outcome variables included agility, dynamic balance, muscular power, cardiorespiratory endurance, inhibitory control, working memory, cognitive flexibility, psychological resilience, self-regulation, and perceived stress. Assessments were conducted at baseline, 6 weeks, and 12 weeks. Data were analyzed using Mixed MANOVA and Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons. Results Significant Group × Time interaction effects were found across all physical, cognitive, and psychological outcomes ( p < 0.001). Compared with the TPEG and CG, the SMATG showed greater improvements in agility, dynamic balance, standing broad jump performance, Estimated VO₂peak, inhibitory control, working memory, cognitive flexibility, psychological resilience, and self-regulation, as well as greater reductions in perceived stress. Moderate-to-large effect sizes were observed across multidimensional outcomes. Conclusion The findings suggest that structured school-based martial arts training may be a promising approach for supporting multiple physical, cognitive, and psychological outcomes in adolescents.

items.title: Musculoskeletal Symptoms Among Agricultural Workers in Rural Communities of Loja, Ecuador
items.abstract: Background: Musculoskeletal symptoms (MSS) are among the most common occupational health problems worldwide and disproportionately affect agricultural workers because of the physical demands of their work. However, evidence on MSS prevalence among farmers in Ecuador remains limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of MSS and examine its association with selected sociodemographic and occupational factors among agricultural workers in rural communities in Loja, Ecuador. Methods: A descriptive, analytical, cross-sectional study was conducted among 103 farmers using the Standardized Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ). Descriptive statistics were used to estimate the 12-month prevalence of MSS, and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess associations with sociodemographic and occupational variables. Results: A high prevalence of MSS was observed, particularly in the lower back (78.6%), knees (64.1%), and neck (58.3%). Overweight was significantly associated with lower back pain and marginally associated with neck pain. No significant associations were found between MSS prevalence and occupational exposure variables, such as working posture or weekly working hours. Conclusions: MSS are highly prevalent among agricultural workers in rural Ecuador. These findings highlight the need for preventive occupational health strategies to reduce musculoskeletal risk in agricultural settings.

items.title: NAIL-C: A Neurodiversity-Adaptive Framework for Inclusive Language Learning in the Age of AI
items.abstract: Theories of second language acquisition (SLA) have largely assumed that learners can access input and take part in interaction under broadly stable sensory, cognitive, and emotional conditions. Neurodiversity shows that these conditions vary within and across learners, while large language models (LLMs) now mediate much everyday language work. This conceptual article argues that the relationship between regulated access, communicative competence, and AI mediation remains under-theorized in SLA. Through a theoretical synthesis of SLA, neurodiversity scholarship, ecological and distributed cognition, multimodality, and research on AI-mediated communication, it proposes NAIL-C, a neurodiversity-adaptive framework with five interdependent components: Neurodiversity-Centered Design, Adaptive Regulation, Tolerable and Adaptive Input, Learning as Dynamic Alignment, and Multimodality-Adaptive Communicative Competence. The framework treats regulated access as a boundary condition on acquisition, defines communicative competence so that multimodal and variable participation can count as evidence, and positions AI as a potential regulatory scaffold that requires human oversight. NAIL-C complements Universal Design for Learning by offering an SLA-specific account of usable input and competence. The article specifies falsifiable predictions and outlines implications for assessment, pedagogy, and research.

items.title: Nanocochleates as Smart Lipidic Nanocarriers for Improved Anticancer Therapy Recent Advances and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Cancer therapy is frequently limited by poor aqueous solubility, inadequate bioavailability, rapid degradation, nonspecific distribution, systemic toxicity, and multidrug resistance, creating a need for advanced drug-delivery systems.Nanocochleates have emerged as promising lipidic nanocarriers characterized by compact, tightly packed multilamellar structures formed through interactions between negatively charged phospholipids and divalent cations, particularly calcium ions.Their distinctive architecture provides drug protection, improved retention, and potential for sustained and controlled release.This review discusses the development of nanocochleates as smart nanocarriers for improved anticancer therapy, with emphasis on their fundamental characteristics, composition, formation mechanisms, preparation approaches, and physicochemical characterization.Their potential for delivering conventional anticancer agents and poorly bioavailable natural compounds is discussed, including applications involving doxorubicin, fisetin, paclitaxel, curcumin, quercetin, and resveratrol.Particular attention is given to passive and active tumor targeting, folate-, antibody-, peptide-, and tumor-microenvironment-based strategies, as well as pH-, redox-, enzyme-, and reactive oxygen species-responsive systems.The review further highlights nanocochleateenabled combination therapy, drug/gene co-delivery, immunotherapy integration, and potential approaches for overcoming multidrug resistance.Safety, toxicity, biocompatibility, formulation reproducibility, scale-up, quality control, regulatory requirements, and clinical translation are also considered.Future perspectives include multifunctional and theranostic nanocochleates, artificial intelligence-assisted formulation optimization, Quality by Design, personalized nanomedicine, and scalable manufacturing.Overall, nanocochleates represent a promising platform for precision cancer therapy, although rigorous in vivo validation, standardized manufacturing, long-term safety assessment, and well-designed clinical studies are required to establish their therapeutic and translational value and demonstrate clear advantages over established nanomedicine platforms in efficacy, safety, stability, and patientspecific therapeutic outcomes.

items.title: Nanosponge-Based Topical Delivery Systems for Psoriasis: Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory skin disorder characterized by abnormal keratinocyte proliferation, epidermal hyperplasia, and persistent inflammation.Although topical therapy remains an important approach for mild-to-moderate psoriasis, conventional formulations are often associated with poor drug solubility, inadequate skin penetration, rapid drug release, limited skin retention, and potential adverse effects.Nanotechnologybased delivery systems have therefore emerged as promising strategies for improving localized and controlled drug delivery.Among these, nanosponges are porous, three-dimensional, cross-linked nanocarriers capable of incorporating active pharmaceutical ingredients and functioning as drug reservoirs.Their unique architecture offers advantages including enhanced solubility, drug protection, controlled release, and improved skin deposition.This review discusses the potential of nanosponge-based topical delivery systems for psoriasis, with emphasis on their pharmaceutical characteristics, types, preparation strategies, drug-loading mechanisms, and physicochemical characterization.Current evidence on nanosponge formulations containing antipsoriatic agents, including clobetasol propionate, curcumin, caffeine, and sulfasalazine, is critically examined with respect to drug release, skin delivery, and preclinical therapeutic outcomes.The incorporation of nanosponges into topical gels and hydrogels is also discussed as an approach to improve residence time, spreadability, and localized drug delivery.Despite encouraging preclinical findings, challenges remain regarding formulation optimization, batch reproducibility, dermal safety, scaleup, regulatory requirements, and clinical validation.Future development may focus on targeted and stimuli-responsive nanosponges, combination therapy, quality-by-design approaches, artificial intelligence-assisted optimization, and scalable manufacturing.Overall, nanosponges represent a promising platform for developing localized, sustained, and patient-friendly topical therapies for psoriasis.

items.title: Natural language processing and intelligent decision optimization technology for user feedback in hotel management
items.abstract: With the deep penetration of artificial intelligence technology in the hotel industry, natural language processing and reinforcement learning algorithms offer new approaches to solving the issues of inefficient user feedback analysis and lagging decision optimization in hotel management. Addressing the characteristics of hotel user feedback, specifically its colloquial nature and semantic complexity, and the inability of traditional manual analysis methods to meet the demands of large-scale, high-timeliness analysis, this study proposes a novel approach. It employs a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer model based on whole-word masking to enhance the semantic representation capabilities of colloquial Chinese feedback. This is combined with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network to capture long-range temporal dependencies within the text context. Finally, by integrating Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient, an intelligent optimization decision-making module is constructed. The synthesis of these three components establishes an intelligent optimization technology for hotel management driven by user feedback. The comparative experiment results showed that the technology outperformed the comparative model in terms of hotel user feedback analysis and core indicators of management decision optimization. The accuracy of sentiment classification was 92.37%, the accuracy of problem extraction was 89.64%, and the final accuracy of positive, neutral, and negative sentiment text classification was stable at 93.5%, 89%, and 92.5%, respectively. From this, the proposed technology can capture the core semantics and problem characteristics of hotel user feedback, enhance the scientific nature of hotel management decisions and the precision of service optimization, and provide a scientific basis for the intelligent and data-driven transformation of the hotel industry, as well as word-of-mouth improvement and customer retention.

items.title: Navigating Professional Code of Conduct Among Undergraduate Dental Students in Pakistan: A Qualitative Study
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Professionalism in dentistry extends beyond technical competence to include accountability, respect for patients and colleagues, non‐maleficence, informed consent, communication, fairness, and conduct consistent with professional standards. In Pakistan, these expectations are shaped by international bioethical principles, national professional regulation, and local social and religious contexts. Aim To explore undergraduate dental students' experiences of, or observations of, events they perceived as unethical or inconsistent with professional conduct during clinical/workplace learning, and to understand the forms and meanings of these experiences. Methods A qualitative narrative inquiry was conducted over 6 months (November 2020–April 2021) at two dental colleges in Peshawar, Pakistan, one public and one private. Purposive sampling was used to recruit clinically exposed undergraduate dental students. Fifty students were approached and 37 participated in semi‐structured interviews. Data were analyzed using Template Analysis. The report follows the COREQ framework and makes the analytic, reflexive, and trustworthiness procedures explicit. Results Participants had a mean age of 20.9 ± 1.96 years (range 17–25); 29 (78.4%) were female and 8 (21.6%) male. Four interconnected themes were identified: unprofessionalism, harassment, poor communication, and discrimination. The accounts included concerns about infection control, empathy, accountability for clinical error, dishonesty, physical/verbal/emotional harassment, inadequate instruction, failures of informed consent, abuse of power, victimization, and targeting. Conclusion Students' accounts point primarily to breaches of professional conduct and to tensions between formal ethical expectations and the hidden curriculum of clinical learning. Professionalism education should therefore be embedded longitudinally in dental curricula and reinforced through faculty role‐modeling, safe reporting pathways, supervised clinical practice, and context‐sensitive ethical reasoning that can hold universal duties together with legitimate cultural and religious considerations.

items.title: Negotiating professional identity in the creative industries: the REC framework for Human–AI creative work
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes professional identity in the creative industries. Although prior research has largely emphasized the technological capabilities and industry-level implications of AI, limited attention has been devoted to how creative professionals themselves interpret and negotiate its consequences for creativity, authorship, and career development. Design/methodology/approach An inductive qualitative design is conducted based on 40 semi-structured interviews with professionals from the Italian audiovisual industry, including actors, directors, screenwriters, technicians, and AI experts. Data were analyzed using the Gioia methodology. Findings Findings show that AI does not simply support creative work but disrupts established understandings of what it means to be a creative professional. Three interconnected forms of identity work emerge: resisting, extending, and crafting (REC). While some participants defend the human and symbolic foundations of creativity, others embrace AI as a source of experimentation and new skill formation. More critically, AI also generates identity ambiguity and fragmentation, blurring boundaries between human originality, technological assistance, and professional legitimacy. Originality/value This work addresses an important gap in AI and creative work research by shifting attention from technological adoption to the identity-level consequences of AI. Through a unique and heterogeneous dataset spanning multiple creative occupations, the study introduces the REC framework and conceptualizes AI as a disruptive identity force that simultaneously enables, threatens, and redefines career sustainability.

Modern cyber threats have surpassed the capabilities of conventional security systems, requiring organizations and people to develop new methods for safeguarding digital resources. The research examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) transforms modern cybersecurity and forensic operations through its ability to create smarter and faster adaptive security solutions. The new generation of cybersecurity systems depends on AI technologies, which include machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and anomaly detection. The tools outperform traditional manual methods by detecting and handling complex threats at a higher speed and effectiveness. The research examines multiple AI-based security solutions, which include sophisticated intrusion detection systems, automated malware identification, intelligence-based threat tracking, and AI-supported forensic analysis. The implementation of AI in security domains requires immediate resolution of multiple operational, ethical, and legal issues. AI technology will transform cybersecurity through predictive forensic capabilities, autonomous defense systems, and adaptive security systems in the future. The new security solutions will enhance organizational defenses while improving incident response efficiency and building digital infrastructure trust in complex systems.

items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence is reshaping human resource management, influencing how organizations engage with employees across the entire lifecycle. This chapter examines the use of intelligent HR systems that draw on machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics to create more adaptive and responsive practices. These technologies support personalized onboarding, refine talent acquisition, and enable continuous learning by identifying evolving skill needs. At the same time, their application extends to employee well-being, where data-driven insights help organizations respond more effectively to workforce dynamics. The benefits are evident in improved engagement and reduced administrative workload, alongside more informed decision-making. In contrast, concerns related to algorithmic bias, data privacy, and the limits of automation remain significant. Sustained value depends on ethical governance, transparency, and a balanced integration of human judgment.

items.title: ODC-Agents: Multi-Agent Shift-Left Defect Triage, Benchmarked from Manual ODC to LLMs
items.abstract: When an automated test fails, someone must decide whether the product or the test is at fault. This paper evaluates four generations of that triage decision on the same real data: manual ODC (human triage as ground truth), statistical cross-cube analysis as practised in the 1990s (implemented in APL and run through a Python-to-APL connector), AutoODC-style text classifiers (2011), and a zero-shot LLM triage agent that never sees the labels. The data are 9,961 anonymised failures from five weeks of automated system testing of Android enterprise devices, of which 815 were triaged by the vendor's engineers as genuine product defects. All stages are scored on held-out later weeks with identical metrics, a 0-50% log-noise stress test and a what-if analysis. No generation dominates: cross-cube analysis is precise but misses most defects, text classifiers and the LLM catch most defects but raise many false alarms because identical failure messages carry opposite labels in different suites, and ODC-Agents, a multi-agent design that fuses cube history with LLM reading under an independent evaluator agent, reaches 0.94 precision and a PR-AUC above either component. A supervised random forest trained on the human triage is the strongest single model. The results support a multi-agent architecture in which statistical history, semantic reading and human triage each play a distinct, measurable role, with an independent evaluator agent.

items.title: Offline Healthcare Chatbot using Local LLM and Docker for Privacy-Preserving AI
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have penetrated the surprisingly broad scope of medical applications in the last few years. applications, starting with simple symptom checker up to chronic disease monitoring and educational services to patients [1, 13, 14]. The overwhelming most of these systems, but, nevertheless, rely on cloud-hosted inference endpoints, which raises three interconnected issues: sensitive health information gets sent to the servers that cannot be controlled by the user, the system fails when the internet connectivity is poor or unavailable, and regulatory compliance becomes challenging to ensure [5, 11]. In this paper, the design, implementation, and evaluation of a healthcare chatbot will be introduced, where the software is fully executed on the user's own computer in the form of a collection of Docker containers that can be run at a single command on either Windows, macOS, or Linux. Ollama is used to do language model inference, and it has an open-source model and a local HTTP endpoint. A Python Flask program is placed between the user interfaces and the model and this handles session context, input validation, prompt engineering. Both a single-page application (rendered in a browser) and a native desktop GUI share the same REST API, both of them maintain the communication on 127.0.0.1 all the time. The results of the experiment prove successful cross-platform deployment, the absence of external network traffic, reasonable response latency on commodity hardware (2 4 seconds on a quad-core processor with 16 GB RAM to represent queries in health information), and consistent and relevant responses to exemplary queries in health information. The article shows a viable and implementable prototype of privacy-conscious, offline healthcare chatbots constructed solely out of open-source software.

items.title: On Multilingual Text Summarization: A Review of Model Architectures, Techniques, and Research Gaps
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of multilingual digital content has intensified demand for automated text summarization systems that can operate across diverse languages. Yet the architectural and methodological foundations of this domain remain dispersed across individual studies. This paper presents a systematic literature review of multilingual text summarization research in Natural Language Processing, with particular attention to model architectures, multilingual enabling techniques, and existing research gaps. Following a PRISMA-guided review protocol, 47 studies published between 2017 and 2026 were identified, screened, and synthesized from major scholarly databases using predefined eligibility and quality assessment criteria. The analysis shows that the literature is dominated by four dominant architectural paradigms: multilingual sequence-to-sequence models, large language models, adapter-based models, and hybrid architectures, with a recent shift toward large language model-based approaches. Across these studies, multilingual capability is primarily achieved through pre-training and transfer learning, with support from parameter-efficient adaptation and data augmentation. The review further identified four persistent limitation categories: low-resource language underrepresentation; dataset and benchmark constraints; evaluation limitations dominated by ROUGE overreliance; and generalization and scalability challenges, manifested as the curse of multilinguality. These findings indicate that current progress in the field is largely driven by scaling existing models rather than resolving structural multilingual limitations, particularly those related to data availability and model architecture. This paper provides a consolidated view of architectural and methodological trends and offers a structured, informed basis for future research on equitable multilingual summarization, particularly for low-resource languages.

items.title: Optimized Artificial Intelligence Framework for Retail Sales Prediction and Decision Support
items.abstract: The retail industry operates in a highly dynamic and competitive environment characterized by fluctuating consumer behavior, seasonal demand variations, and market uncertainties.Accurate sales forecasting is essential for effective inventory management, demand planning, pricing strategies, and overall business decision-making.However, traditional statistical forecasting techniques often fail to capture the complex nonlinear and temporal relationships present in largescale retail datasets, resulting in limited predictive performance.To address these challenges, this study proposes an optimized Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Decision Support System (DSS) for retail sales forecasting using hybrid machine learning techniques.The proposed framework integrates multiple machine learning models to leverage their complementary strengths in capturing both linear and nonlinear patterns from historical sales data.Advanced optimization techniques are incorporated for hyperparameter tuning to enhance model accuracy, reduce overfitting, and improve computational efficiency.The system employs intelligent forecasting mechanisms capable of processing large volumes of retail data and generating accurate, scalable, and near real-time sales predictions.Furthermore, the integration of the forecasting framework within a decision support environment enables retailers to obtain actionable insights for inventory control, supply chain management, promotional planning, and resource allocation.The proposed AI-based DSS aims to improve forecasting reliability, operational efficiency, and strategic decisionmaking in retail organizations.By combining hybrid machine learning models with optimization algorithms, the framework provides a robust and adaptive solution for modern retail sales forecasting, ultimately contributing to enhanced business performance, reduced operational costs, and improved customer satisfaction.
